Use case: `session.created` provisions a Postgres database and MinIO bucket scoped to the worktree's branch slug; `worktree.removed` would tear them down.

One specific ask on the payload: the current proposal has `worktree.removed: { directory }` firing **after** directory cleanup. Our teardown script calls `git -C $directory rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` to get the branch name — that fails once the directory is gone. Either include `branch` in the payload (same as `worktree.created`) or fire before directory cleanup. Either change makes the hook usable for external resource teardown without requiring the branch name to be encoded in the directory path.

Reference: [`worktree-up.sh`](https://github.com/guillempuche/batuda/blob/main/.claude/hooks/worktree-up.sh) · [`worktree-down.sh`](https://github.com/guillempuche/batuda/blob/main/.claude/hooks/worktree-down.sh)

Sharing a concrete migration log from a Claude Code → opencode port as data for this issue:

**Translated cleanly:** `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse` block/approve → `tool.execute.before` (bonus: also covers MCP tools). Formatters (biome, dprint) → native `formatter` config. `SessionStart` for new sessions → `session.created`.

**Needed workarounds:** Soft `systemMessage` reminders (lingui extract, domain schema migration check) → `experimental.session.compacting` (reaches the AI but only at compaction time, not per-edit). Branch context → `experimental.chat.system.transform`.

**No equivalent found:** `WorktreeRemove` teardown (drop provisioned DB + storage bucket), `SubagentStop` TypeScript check, `Stop` hook re-entry.

Reference: [`.claude/settings.json`](https://github.com/guillempuche/batuda/blob/main/.claude/settings.json) (source hooks)

Claude Code also provides this feature under the name [path specific rules](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory#path-specific-rules).

For now, the closest workaround I found is to instruct the agent to lazy-load the rules using `@` references in `AGENTS.md` ([example](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/rules.mdx#manual-instructions-in-agentsmd)).
Note that this is model-driven, not a deterministic extension matcher.

Sorry about the late reply to this: yes, the automations are implemented server-side, so create/delete of automations, run history/findings, and on-demand execution are available through the HTTP API and generated JS SDK.

With `opencode serve` running, an external process can run an automation with:
```
POST /automation/{automationID}/run?directory=...
```

To trigger compaction:
```
POST /session/{sessionID}/summarize?directory=...
```
This accepts the provider/model in its request body, so an external process could audit idle sessions and compact eligible ones directly.

The current branch does not already implement the condition “idle for N seconds and never compacted”, so that check would still need to live in the external auditing process for now.

Hi @rekram1-node — I drafted an RFC that tries to agree on shape first, per your note on this issue ("I'd rather agree on the shape here before a PR: how it surfaces as tools, where recorded flows live relative to skills, and the permission model for actions").

It's up as a draft PR: #33082 (docs only, adds `rfcs/computer-use.md`). Cross-references this issue plus #20490 / #20917 / #26772 / #30755.

A few places where I made calls and would value a sanity check before going further:

- **Permission model** — one prompt per session with `max_steps_per_task: 50` budget, no per-action prompts (chose this over Codex's per-action model on UX grounds).
- **Core-native vs plugin** — went Core-native, behind `computer_use.enabled: false` experimental flag. You flagged on #20490 that you wanted this closed, which made me cautious — happy to flip to plugin-first if you'd rather see it land there and graduate.
- **UI-TARS-1.5-7B** as the recommended local adapter (Apache-2.0, OSWorld 42.5, beats Claude 3.7 and CUA). If opencode already has a preferred local VLM story, I'd rather align than propose a new one.

I'll wait on feedback here before pushing anything else. Happy to iterate on the doc.
